Only get this game if you know how to play it or a game similar to it. I got this game a few years ago and only now decided to play it and was faced with extreme confusion. It gave you a tutorial on how to connect your city to the highway, but that was literally it. I had no idea what to do from there on. I had to guess what to do.
If you're game requires you to go onto youtube to find a tutorial to even just start it, then it's a bad game.
to hard no tutorial, at least help the player a bit

The game could be fun! However it is impossible to pick up, you have to have so many things such as electricity and water etc. That isn't too bad however there is no tutorial to help you understand how that works and I guess there is a giant paragraph but that is so long and will take at least a couple hours to read and understand. In conclusion, the game could be fun but it is really hard to understand and way to many things to keep track of. It could be better if there was an option to turn the power and water etc off!

claims.claim: This cohort reports frustration with the Paradox account login and launcher requirements.

citations.review_text: Spent more time on setting up the game than playing it. Absolutely do not recommend you will constantly be screamed at to buy DLC (Literally is everywhere: on map selection, on menu etc.) or make a paradox account.

Incredibly fun and addicting. Got ~40hrs on record on a copy of the game I had before deciding it was worth buying.

I've also seen some people complain about the paradox launcher; just use: 
[b]"..\steamapps\common\Cities_Skylines\Cities.exe" %command%[/b] in Launch Options to launch right into the game instead. [i](".." obviously being wherever you keep Steam installed).[/i]
i bought ts on steam but when i launch and signed up for paradox it says i have to buy it again and when i try more it wants a subscibtion. f you!

Spent more time fighting the paradox launcher ... finally blocked that spyware only to hate the UI, sound effects and ... well pretty much everting. Having grown up with Sim City, this game confuses me ... not the concept but the cartoon graphics style and the default settings for sound (awful music and all that clicking) ... and the push towards connecting online,  end especially that blue bird thing!!!  I cannot be bothered with the UI friction these choices have made. There may be some real complexity in a game from this generation (cf Sim City) ... but it feels like it was designed for a much younger audience.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Established cities experience traffic gridlocks and growth stagnation, though mods help address these challenges.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that end-game and established cities suffer from stagnation, traffic implosions, and difficulties with continued growth.

citations.review_text: I love starting new Cities but I find it’s hard once a City is established to grow and gets quite boring. Still one of my favourite games.

It's not a bad game per say, but the DLC structure of it is slop. The base game comes with just a few maps, enough to sort of re-live the SimCity gameplay. I think if SimCity 2013 wasn't such an utter failure by EA, this game wouldn't have anywhere near the playerbase it has. But hey, it was perfect timing for Cities:Skylines and they got rewarded for it. 

The beginning stages of each map are always fun in that you have to build correctly with the limited resources that you have. Mid game is also relatively good, you are managing the water/electricity/traffic to the best of your abilities and it works out for the most part. In the end-game things become significantly stagnant, traffic implodes on itself, fires run rampant even with firehouses placed everywhere because of the traffic and the whole thing becomes a post-capitalism dystopia pretty much every time. People say that mods and DLCs help alleviate some of that, but I've just been a base game enjoyer for many years now and don't really feel like getting into all of those extra additions. 

Overall, I'd still say it's a pretty good game if you are in the mood for some SimCity town building simulator. I still hop on every once in a while just to relive it. I'd probably recommend watching others play it before buying it unless on sale though. It fits a niche, but would I recommend it to everyone? Absolutely not. The base game just feels like you are missing out on the vast majority of the experience that they drip fed into the game over years of DLC content. And with all of that content being >$100, it really just feels like a nickel and diming effort that isn't really worth pursuing. Will it scratch the city building itch, yes, for a time until you get to the late-game. But if you aren't a hobbyist of this genre it sort of fizzles out by the 6 hour mark of every town you make. 

Still a good game, but closer to an 7 or and 8/10, so leaving a negative review even though I have enjoyed it.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that managing road traffic, designing intersections, and dealing with gridlocks present a significant and challenging aspect of gameplay.

citations.review_text:
After seeing that Cities: Skylines 2 is still being “finished” - although I’m glad it’s in a much better state now than it was at launch - I finally decided [i](bought some free time)[/i] to check out how the original game holds up after all these years.

Just as it did when it first came out, this city-building simulator can still swallow up hours of your life. For a casual player like me, it has become the definitive city-building experience: during the first hour, you have to carefully balance your finances to avoid slipping into the red. After that, you’re free to decide which of your city’s problems you feel like tackling.

Without fail, two or three hours later I find myself hopelessly stuck designing road interchanges, trying to create the most efficient routes for traffic. Then I spend another hour admiring the fact that I’ve somehow managed to make everything even worse. Overall, the simulation, objectives, and available tools are all designed in a way that makes the game incredibly difficult to put down. Despite having played it before, I immediately lost another 4.5 hours to it.

A subscription granting access to all the DLC is available at a perfectly reasonable price. I can’t say that every piece of content is particularly “high-quality,” but there is now so much of it that the constant “don’t forget to check out this new building” notifications start getting a little annoying after a couple of hours. Still, I think there’s something here for everyone - especially those blessed with a good imagination and plenty of free time.

City builders may not be the most popular genre in gaming, but it’s both impressive [i](and a little sad)[/i] that even after 11 years, Cities: Skylines still has no real competition. And it still plays wonderfully.

''City skylines is hand down the best city-building simulator out there. The zoning mechanics, the industrial specializations (like oil and faming), and the traffic management system give total control over your dream city. It can be challenging when managing gridlocks or sewage issues, but that' what makes it so addictive and satisfying. A solid 10/10 for any strategy game fan!"

best city builder game of its time. the game's okay vanilla, excellent with the huge library of free steam workshop mods and assets, and outstanding with the couple DLCs i'd consider essential to the game. had a city of abt 400k w/ 500+ steam workshop assets on an older build from 2017 that ran really well even into 2026. great game if you love customization- you can tinker with everything in this game. just be warned that you may need to troubleshoot as much as you customize... game breaks every now and then when paradox updates it, but it eventually fixes itself through troubleshoot or just waiting for a patch. also, the traffic AI is kinda stupid. they use just one lane on a 6 lane highway and will cut across those same 6 lanes to exit. time will only tell if i can say the same good things for c:s2, but at the time of writring this, it has a long way to go. despite the traffic AI issues and occasional crashes, c:s1 is my favourite game of all time, and has really helped me explore my passion for transporation engineering and urban planning (: would recommend buying in 2026. especially during a sale. base game + DLCs for mass transit, industries, parklife, after dark, and snowfall are what i'd recommend

First of all, I'd like to say, that if this game was good, I'd love it. I really like the concept, the style, the idea, but this game was built for rage baiting. I mean, the main thing that one has to do when building a city is manage traffic and the flow of goods. You could be a proffesional city planner, and fail at this task. Not because you're stupid or incapable of these two things, but because the game has one purpose, only one: create new ways, so it can ♥♥♥♥ with you. Let me tell you about my situation: 
I've built myself a city with 3 main areas: residential/commercial place, ore industry, oil industry. I've placed warehouses WITH RAILWAY CONNECTION for each and every material (such as commercial goods, zoned ore industry products, zoned oil industry products, metals, glass, petroleum, plastics). I obviusly placed these warehouses close to their desired production/consumer place, and connected them all to the outside (by rails)...... And exepct for a few trains, nothing happened. Buissneses started complaining about not having enough goods to sell, trucks started exporting stuff themselves, eventually the prodiction buildings were complaining about not having enough costumers, and buildings that would transform said products complained about not having sufficient supply (because all of the trucks from the buildings that produced things, were out "exporting" products instead of giving said products to the warehouses I've placed aproximately 30 meters away, so that warehouse could export it by train, AND in the rare cases, when trucks were willing to transfer these products to the warehouses, no trains came (and yes, I did connect them properly). Soooo, I placed cargo train terminals..... Trains came flooding in. You'd think: that's that, problem solved, BUT NOOOOO. i've placed these cargo train terminals (3 of them total) specificaly right next to the 3 main "centers" of my city (the commercial zone, oil and ore industry). AND GUESS WHAT. The one next to the…

Started the game with a simple dream: build a clean, efficient city where everyone is happy.

Two hours later, the roads are gridlocked, sewage is flowing directly into the drinking water and I’m pretending not to notice.
 
I raised taxes to fix the budget, everyone complained....
I lowered taxes, the city went bankrupt....
I built public transport, nobody used it....
I demolished half the city to add a motorway, and somehow traffic got worse?

The citizens constantly complain about traffic, noise and rubbish, despite living in a house I personally placed between a motorway, an incinerator, a landfill and six wind turbines. Honestly, some people are never happy.
I genuinely spent 3 hours designing the perfect motorway junction in and around a city, only for one confused lorry to ignore it and block the entire city

10/10. Thanks to this game, I’m now fully qualified to run for my local council.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the vanilla base game has limitations and that purchasing downloadable content or utilizing workshop items is necessary to experience the game fully.

citations.review_text:
This game is real good as a city simulation and very, but VERY addictive and the modding community is very active and thousand UGC are available.
But, Paradox obliges, you are fastly limited if you don't buy DLC or sub to workshops items, the vanilla game rapidly shows its limits unfortunately, and CS2 is  far from getting optimized, so i would recommend this game instead, the graphisms are not cutting edge, but they haven't olden that much since 2015.
And modding the game is a little tricky, especially if you don't have skyve installed to check the compatiblity reports. I got issues of crashing at load/save when playing with mods. And the waiting time between major updates can be long.

A modern classic, and the spiritual successor to SimCity, City Skylines is a great game. With infinite replayability (aided by the expansive mod collection), this game is my most played on steam and definitely worth picking up. The only problem is that there are too many DLC, and some of them (including all the radio stations) aren't worth picking up, but there are also some that basically necessary to be able to play the game to its fullest
